FACT the file has one `sorry` in `putnam_2022_a5`, and the statement is `IsGreatest` over Alice strategies on a 2022-square board.
FACT `ConformsToStrategy` constrains only even indices, so Alice's moves are fixed by `s` and Bob's moves are free.
FACT the conclusion `∃ gh x, g = gh ++ [x] ∧ n ≤ xᶜ.ncard` quantifies over the last state of every conforming prefix, not only terminal states.
INFER the statement is equivalent to the real game claim: Alice can force at least 290 uncovered squares at the end, and Bob can hold her to 290. Uncovered counts are nonincreasing along play, so every prefix inherits the terminal bound. The prefix quantifier adds no loophole.
FACT no trivial witness exists. The lower bound needs an explicit Alice strategy `s` with an invariant that holds against every Bob continuation. The upper bound needs, for every `s`, a Bob line that ends with at most 290 uncovered squares.
INFER a Lean proof requires formalizing both halves of the Putnam 2022 A5 game analysis over `Set (Fin 2022)` states with arbitrary-length game lists. That is a large development, far beyond a short edit.
PLAN I am not going to write a partial proof, since the rules forbid `sorry` and I have no verified path to a complete one.

I give up. The file is unchanged, and the theorem remains unproven. The claim is a genuine game-theoretic result, and I did not find a shortcut in the statement that would make the proof routine.
